claims.statement: EU battery producers or their producer-responsibility organisations must finance end-of-life collection, treatment and recycling and select waste-management operators, establishing a real regulated payer and procurement process.

The European Commission reported in December 2025 that EU black-mass treatment capacity was largely under-used and that access to feedstock, rather than a generic shortage of recycler capacity, was the immediate industry constraint.

Relevant cross-border waste shipments can require prior notification and consent, an effective contract, and a financial guarantee or equivalent insurance, so a reservation is not itself a compliant treatment route.

Direct substitutes already connect battery owners, recyclers and service providers: Recircle.market launched an EU-funded circular-battery marketplace in 2026, while ReBattery advertises chemistry matching, licensed-recycler quotes, logistics and compliance documentation.
Large actors also substitute bilateral contracting for an exchange: BASF and Stena entered a black-mass purchase agreement covering collection, pre-treatment and refining.

A narrower feedstock-routing and compliant quote/documentation service may address fragmentation, but public evidence does not establish demand for forward capacity reservations or the proposed per-tonne fee.

contrary_evidence: The Commission's December 2025 RESourceEU plan says relevant EU recycling capacity is largely under-utilised and feedstock access is the challenge, directly opposing the v1 assumption of broad capacity scarcity.
Recircle.market and ReBattery already offer overlapping marketplace, chemistry-matching, recycler-discovery and documentation functions.
BASF and Stena's bilateral purchase agreement shows that strategic feedstock and refining capacity can be secured through closed industrial partnerships rather than a neutral exchange.
Cross-border waste movements can require notification, consent, contracts and financial guarantees, increasing transaction friction and limiting what a software reservation alone can deliver.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: obtain one licensed recycler and one producer-responsibility organisation or battery generator in a single domestic corridor before attempting cross-border routing; direct competitors already claim recycler networks and EU reach.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Not evidenced. The v1 path assumed one million reserved tonnes and 30 PLN net per tonne without demand, access or price evidence. A credible path requires observed annual routed tonnes, a defensible take rate, repeat bookings and proof that direct marketplaces and bilateral contracts do not compress the fee.
economics.founder_time: A matching prototype fits within 2-4 hours per day, but licensed-recycler acquisition, chemistry diligence and cross-border compliance are partner-heavy and may exceed the founder's part-time capacity until delegated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unknown. Software matching could be high margin, but technical screening, hazardous-waste documentation, insurance and shipment support may make the service operationally intensive.
economics.payback: Unknown; the previous 15-24 month estimate depended on 50000 reserved tonnes per year, for which no public demand or reservation commitment was found.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated. ReBattery advertises a free assessment and commission-only second-life listings, while no public source supports 20-50 PLN per reserved tonne for treatment-capacity booking.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Regulatory collection and reporting recur, but recycler feedstock shortages and bilateral supply agreements may create long contracts that bypass repeated marketplace booking.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Verified chemistry, acceptance, rejection, route and recovery-document history could improve matching, but only if recycler and generator participation exceeds existing marketplaces.
fingerprint.customer: EU battery producers, producer-responsibility organisations, collectors, industrial battery holders and licensed recyclers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A single-country recycler and producer-responsibility anchor, followed by battery associations and collection contractors; cross-border expansion only after shipment compliance is operational
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Chemistry and location matching, indicative capacity or feedstock requests, compliant quote workflow and treatment-document vault; no claim that a reservation replaces statutory shipment approvals
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A generator or producer-responsibility organisation pays for an accepted compliant treatment route; a recycler commission is payable only where a signed agreement permits it
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A waste holder needs a permitted treatment route or a recycler needs suitable feedstock; current evidence does not show an economy-wide shortage of treatment capacity

founder_fit: Chemistry and route matching suit the founder's data-science and optimisation skills.
The renewable-storage network may provide a small validation channel for industrial batteries.
No plant ownership is required, but recycler contracting and regulated shipment execution require experienced partners and concentrated commercial work.
risks: The core capacity-scarcity premise may be wrong while European recyclers compete for feedstock.
Existing marketplaces and bilateral industrial agreements may control supply before a new entrant can aggregate it.
Acting as a waste broker or arranging shipments may trigger registration, contractual, insurance or country-specific compliance duties.
Chemistry misclassification, damaged-battery transport and rejected loads can create safety and liability exposure.
Part-time founder capacity may be inadequate for simultaneous recycler sales, technical diligence and multi-country compliance.

structure.control_point: verified live recycler acceptance conditions and legally usable treatment commitments
structure.critical_dependency: signed recycler participation plus contracts, permissions and financial assurance required for each applicable waste route

thesis: The evidence does not support a broad forward book premised on scarce EU battery-recycling capacity: the Commission reports under-used capacity and scarce feedstock, and direct marketplaces already exist. The remaining testable wedge is a single-corridor, compliance-aware feedstock-routing and quote workflow that matches chemistry and location, preserves treatment evidence and never represents a reservation as statutory shipment approval. It is viable only if recycler and producer-responsibility partners expose usable inventory and pay for completed routes rather than continuing bilateral procurement.
title: Waste-Battery Recycling Capacity Forward Book
uncertainties: Whether any recycler will expose binding future acceptance capacity to an independent platform
Observed frequency and cost of failed recycler matching by chemistry and geography
Who can lawfully act as notifier or broker in each initial jurisdiction
Reservation, commission and insurance economics per accepted tonne
Whether producer-responsibility procurement rules permit the proposed marketplace channel
